_what: The one default end of every grant of the person's access: it ends when it has gone unused for unused_days (a person's AI, a run share, a key). Each use starts the days again. The number lives only here: Better Auth's refresh token window is rendered from it (tools/better-auth-official/auth.mjs), and a run share's condition row copies it at the moment the share is made, so the person can read it, change it or remove the row and nothing writes it back. Sources: Microsoft Entra refresh tokens 90 days restarted on use (learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/refresh-tokens), Atlassian 3LO 90 days inactive (developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/oauth-2-3lo-apps), old Trillion's shipped passkey sign-in lifetime of 90 days (commit 4189ea6ede, src/sign-in-lifetimes.json).
_check_window_fraction: How often the sweep that ends grants wakes, as a fraction of unused_days: a grant is ended at most this fraction of the window after it should have been (0.01 of 90 days is 21.6 hours late at worst, harmless for access that is forgotten), and the person's wake ledger (trillion-rust src/wake/wake.json ledgers.work, 2000 steps a day) pays one step per wake, so the sweep draws about 1 of 2000 a day instead of the 288 of a five-minute wake.
_ended: What the sweep writes when it withdraws a grant, one record per grant, { grant, ended_at, reason: 'unused' | 'end-passed', unused_days }. The sign-in tool's Connections page reads it to say 'Access ended: not used for 90 days.' A new grant at the same label removes it.

words.ended_unused: Access ended: not used for {days} days.
words.ended_end_passed: Access ended: its end time passed.
words.unjudged: {count} grants have no last use the engine answers, so only their end time is read.
